proof.text: The compact-support comparisons below may be computed on small-etale $D^+$ before their specified pro-etale realization. Their general Noetherian domain applies: in $R=k[t]_{(t)}$ every nonzero element is $t^m$ times a unit, and choosing the smallest order of a nonzero ideal shows it is generated by $t^m$. Thus every ideal is finitely generated, $R$ is Noetherian and a discrete valuation ring in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr], its strict henselization is again a discrete valuation ring, hence Noetherian (every ideal is principal). A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. All lifts over the strict trait and geometric generic point, their compactifications, and their fibres are finite type over these Noetherian affine bases; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes them Noetherian. The finite ring $A$ is a torsion coefficient ring. The bounded-below compact-support candidates of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] therefore agree with the restrictions of the normalized compactification functors in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], whose statement explicitly identifies its $D^+$ restrictions and their normalizations.

proof.text:
Work in the pro-etale realizations specified in [def-trf-deformation-specialization], retaining etale-origin witnesses for the bounded-below intermediate terms. Write $F_r=Rr_!$, $S_V=\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde V}$, $c_V=\operatorname{can}_V$, $E_r=\mathrm{BC}_{!,r}$, and $e_V=\varepsilon_{a_V}:F_{a_V}\omega_V\to A_s$. Composition identifications are suppressed only in the formulas below, always using the specified ones. Put $\tau_h=\eta_{h,A_U}:A_U\to F_hA_T$, using proper coincidence, and let $p_h:F_h\omega_T\to\omega_U$ be the exceptional-counit part of the pushforward in [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]. Thus $h_*\alpha=p_h\circ F_h(\alpha)\circ\tau_h$. By [def-trf-admissibility], exceptional composition is the conjugate of compact-support composition for the composite adjunction. Its counit is explicitly the composite counit in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. With the dualizing identification of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], this gives
$$e_U\circ F_{a_U}(p_h)=e_T.$$
Consequently, if $t_V(\gamma)=e_V\circ F_{a_V}(\gamma)$, then
$$t_U(h_*\alpha)=t_T(\alpha)\circ F_{a_U}(\tau_h).\tag{1}$$
This follows by substituting the displayed pushforward and applying functoriality; it also gives the same formula for $h_0$ on the special fibres.

source.place: §1.3.2(b),(c), Example 1.3.3(b); compact-support composition as in Stacks Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition)

proof.text:
For $V=T,U$, define
$$J_V=E_{a_V,A_V}\circ F_{a_{V_0}}(c_V):F_{a_{V_0}}A_{V_0}\longrightarrow S_sF_{a_V}A_V.$$
Here $S_s=\operatorname{sp}_D$ and $c_s:A_s\to S_sA_s$ is the invertible map in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. The adjoint of $\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde V}(\gamma)$ under $F_{a_{V_0}}\dashv Ra_{V_0}^!$ is, exactly by that definition,
$$\sigma_V(\gamma)=c_s^{-1}\circ S_s(e_V)\circ E_{a_V,\omega_V}\circ F_{a_{V_0}}(S_V\gamma)\circ F_{a_{V_0}}(c_V).$$
Naturality of $E_{a_V}$ at $\gamma:A_V\to\omega_V$ rewrites this as
$$\sigma_V(\gamma)=c_s^{-1}\circ S_s(t_V(\gamma))\circ J_V.\tag{2}$$
The source and target of the final adjunction are constructible finite-Tor; the intermediate terms in this formula are used only with bounded-below compact support.

source.place: §1.3.2(b),(c), Example 1.3.3(b); compact-support composition as in Stacks Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition)

proof.text:
We first compute the compact-support exchange for the proper lift $\widetilde h$. On the strict trait put $H=R\widetilde h_{D^{\rm sh}*}$ and on the geometric generic fibre put $H_\eta=R\widetilde h_{\bar\eta*}$. Proper compact support is ordinary direct image, using the identity-open compactification. Let $C_i:i_U^*H\xrightarrow\sim Rh_{0*}i_T^*$ be the torsion-coefficient proper base-change isomorphism of [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring], and let $Q:HRj_{T*}\xrightarrow\sim Rj_{U*}H_\eta$ be direct-image composition. The latter exists because $\widetilde h_{D^{\rm sh}}j_T=j_U\widetilde h_{\bar\eta}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. In the definition of $E_h=\mathrm{BC}_{!,h}$, its second arrow is $i_U^*$ of the $j_U$-adjoint of
$$j_U^*HRj_{T*}\xrightarrow{C_j}H_\eta j_T^*Rj_{T*}\xrightarrow{H_\eta\varepsilon_{j_T}}H_\eta.$$
Here $C_j$ is the same torsion-coefficient proper base-change isomorphism at the generic open base change $j_U$. Expanding the ordinary mate definition and using pasting and the identity-mate rule of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies this adjoint with $Q$: its adjunct is exactly the displayed composite, with the adjacent $j_T$ unit and counit cancelled. The same pasting applied to the definition of $B_h=\mathrm{BC}_{*,h}$ gives
$$E_h=i_U^*Q\circ C_i^{-1},\qquad B_h=C_i\circ i_U^*(Q^{-1}).$$
The generic-lift and generic-base-change identifications are inserted on both expressions as in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Thus $E_hB_h=1$ and $B_hE_h=1$, by cancellation of inverse pairs, as maps on $D^+$.

source.place: §1.3.2(b),(c) and Example 1.3.3(b); expanded mate and adjoint calculation

proof.text:
Let $B_h:S_URh_*\to Rh_{0*}S_T$ be ordinary nearby exchange. The nearby-cycle-unit compatibility in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange], applied to the constant sheaf on the total lift, says precisely
$$B_{h,A_T}\circ S_U(\tau_h)\circ c_U=F_{h_0}(c_T)\circ\tau_{h_0}.$$
The units $\tau_h,\tau_{h_0}$ are the ordinary adjunction units, and $F_h=Rh_*$, $F_{h_0}=Rh_{0*}$ here. To see the direction, the exchange $h_0^*S_U\to S_Th^*$ sends $h_0^*c_U$ to $c_T$; its ordinary adjoint evaluated at $A_U$ is the displayed equation. The constant generic input is bounded constructible finite-Tor. Properness is required of the total $D$-morphism $\widetilde h$, as supplied by the item, rather than merely its two fibres. The preceding explicit calculation gives $E_hB_h=1$, hence
$$E_{h,A_T}\circ F_{h_0}(c_T)\circ\tau_{h_0}=S_U(\tau_h)\circ c_U.\tag{3}$$

source.place: §1.3.2(b),(c) and Example 1.3.3(b); expanded mate and adjoint calculation

proof.text:
We compute composition of the specified $E$ maps. For composable lifted arrows $f:V\to W$, $g:W\to Z$, write $F_{\widetilde f},F_{f_\eta}$ for their compact-support functors over the strict trait and geometric generic point. Let $C_{f,i}:i_W^*F_{\widetilde f}\xrightarrow\sim F_{f_0}i_V^*$ and $C_{f,j}:j_W^*F_{\widetilde f}\xrightarrow\sim F_{f_\eta}j_V^*$ be compact-support base change. Define $m_f:F_{\widetilde f}Rj_{V*}\to Rj_{W*}F_{f_\eta}$ to be the $j_W$-adjoint of $F_{f_\eta}(\varepsilon_{j_V})C_{f,j}$, as in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Then $E_f=i_W^*(m_f)C_{f,i}^{-1}$. The explicit base-change/composition compatibility in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] gives
$$C_{gf,i}=F_{g_0}(C_{f,i})C_{g,i}F_{\widetilde f},\quad C_{gf,j}=F_{g_\eta}(C_{f,j})C_{g,j}F_{\widetilde f}.$$
Pasting the $j$-adjunction squares via [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives $m_{gf}=(m_gF_{f_\eta})\circ(F_{\widetilde g}m_f)$: taking its $j_Z$-adjoint yields $F_{g_\eta}F_{f_\eta}(\varepsilon_{j_V})C_{gf,j}$, since the middle $j_W$ unit-counit pair cancels. Substitute into $E_{gf}$ and the first displayed equation, and use naturality of $C_{g,i}$ at $m_f$; this yields $E_{gf}=E_gF_{f!}\circ F_{g_0!}E_f$. Now take $f=h,g=a_U$. The etale/pro-etale composition comparisons agree for this pair by [lem-trf-proper-composition-site-transport], since $h$ is proper. Hence, with precisely the specified pro-etale identifications,
$$E_{a_T,A_T}=E_{a_U,F_hA_T}\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(E_{h,A_T}).\tag{4}$$

source.place: §1.3.2(b),(c) and Example 1.3.3(b); expanded mate and adjoint calculation

proof.text:
Use (4) in the definition of $J_T$, and then (3). Functoriality and naturality of $E_{a_U}$ at $\tau_h:A_U\to F_hA_T$ give the following equality of maps from $F_{a_{U_0}}A_{U_0}$ to $S_sF_{a_T}A_T$:
$$\begin{aligned}
J_T\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(\tau_{h_0})
&=E_{a_U,F_hA_T}\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(E_{h,A_T}\circ F_{h_0}(c_T)\circ\tau_{h_0})\\
&=E_{a_U,F_hA_T}\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(S_U(\tau_h)\circ c_U)\\
&=S_s(F_{a_U}(\tau_h))\circ E_{a_U,A_U}\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(c_U)\\
&=S_s(F_{a_U}(\tau_h))\circ J_U.\tag{5}
\end{aligned}$$
All exchanges here are natural transformations in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]; this calculation uses no exchange for exceptional inverse image of a nearby-cycle output.

source.place: §1.3.2(b),(c), Example 1.3.3(b); compact-support composition as in Stacks Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition)

proof.text:
By (1) on the special fibres, the adjoint of $h_{0*}(\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}\alpha)$ is $\sigma_T(\alpha)\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(\tau_{h_0})$. Substitute (2) and then (5):
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_T(\alpha)\circ F_{a_{U_0}}(\tau_{h_0})
&=c_s^{-1}\circ S_s(t_T(\alpha))\circ S_s(F_{a_U}(\tau_h))\circ J_U\\
&=c_s^{-1}\circ S_s(t_U(h_*\alpha))\circ J_U\\
&=\sigma_U(h_*\alpha).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is (1), and the last is (2). Since the hom bijection of the specified exceptional adjunction for $a_{U_0}$ is injective, the original two Borel--Moore sections are equal. Only $\omega_V=Ra_V^!A_s$ on the original and special fibres occurs as a dualizing object; $S_T\omega_T$ was never identified with $\omega_{T_0}$.

title: Borel–Moore specialization commutes with proper pushforward of lifts
statement:
Use the field $k$, finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and trait $D$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions, def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Let $h:T\to U$ be a proper morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $\widetilde h:\widetilde T\to\widetilde U$ be a proper $D$-morphism of separated finite-type lifts of $h$ in that specialization datum. Write $T_0=\widetilde T_0$, $U_0=\widetilde U_0$ and $h_0:T_0\to U_0$ for the special-fibre morphism. Use the dualizing complexes $\omega_V=Ra_V^!A_s$ of [def-trf-dualizing-complex], and the specified exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility] for $h,h_0$ and these structure morphisms. For every Borel–Moore section $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$, let $h_*\alpha$ and $h_{0*}$ denote the proper pushforward maps on sections of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]. Then the canonically defined Borel–Moore specialization maps satisfy
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde U}(h_*\alpha)
=h_{0*}\bigl(\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde T}(\alpha)\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}(A_{U_0},\omega_{U_0}).$$
This equality uses the nearby-cycle units and compact-support exchange in the definition of specialization and the ordinary unit and exceptional counit in the definition of proper pushforward, with their specified composition identifications. It holds without any assertion that nearby cycles of a dualizing complex themselves are a dualizing complex.
